title: Gradual circuit dissolution and cohort-based fallback for model dependencies
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a safe, observable mechanism for 'dissolving' overloaded or failing circuits at fine granularity (per-model, per-dependency, per-tenant), with staged fallback cohorts and deterministic load-shedding to protect SLOs and preserve critical traffic. Design must cover trip detection, hysteresis, graduated degradation (cohorts), fallback ordering (cached / quantized / smaller models / degraded response), and safety checks for data residency and security-sensitive tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Trip logic supports static thresholds and relative SLO-based thresholds (e.g., baseline-multiplier) and can be applied per-model, per-dependency, and per-tenant
Circuit "dissolve" (partial traffic diversion) implemented as cohort percentages (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with ability to pause/rollback via feature flag
Fallback chain executed in order and respects tenant restrictions (no cross-region or non-compliant fallback for restricted tenants)
Load shedding returns consistent error semantics (HTTP 429 or structured 'degraded' response) and annotated telemetry including reason, cohort, and correlation_id
End-to-end tests and chaos experiments validate SLO protection under synthetic overload and multi-region failover scenarios
Playbook entries added to runbook and alerts trigger on both primary SLO breach probability and unexpected fallback rates
progress_updates: 2026-03-06 - Kickoff: scoped feature. Identified stakeholders: Runtime, Router, Console, Security, Evals.
2026-03-08 - Prototype: router-level percentage diversion implemented in branch feature/circuit-dissolve. Basic cohort plumbing in request path (cohort header).
2026-03-10 - Design review with PM and Security. Decision: fallback chain must check tenant constraints from Tenant Catalog API. Added additional telemetry fields for downstream auditing.
2026-03-12 - Integration work: runtime hook for quantized model variant selection added. Initial integration tests for per-model flags passing locally.

2026-03-13 - QA: created load test harness for cohort percentages and validated that 1%, 5%, 20% diversions produce expected throughput changes; identified race condition when dissolving back to 0% (hysteresis fix planned).
decisions: Use a hybrid trip detector: combine instantaneous metrics (5m error rate, p99 latency) with SLO-breach probability computed against running baseline. A trip triggers if either: error_rate > static_threshold OR breach_probability > 0.8 for the 10m window.
Implement 'dissolution' (gradual circuit opening) as defined cohort percentages that can be configured per-key (model/dependency/tenant). Cohort rollout order: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%.
Fallback chain order: cached response -> quantized/half-precision variant (same model family) -> smaller model family -> partial/summary response -> explicit reject (429 with structured reason).

Hysteresis: require healthy metric window (15m) below threshold to move cohort down; require stable bad window (10m) before moving up one cohort. Immediate full-open only allowed under manual override or critical cascade detection.
Safety: Tenant Catalog determines whether a tenant is allowed to use shared fallback models or cross-region fallbacks. Default for regulated tenants: no cross-region or public-model fallbacks.
Observability: add metrics 'circuit_cohort_percent', 'fallback_invocations_by_step', 'fallback_latency_overhead', and an SLO-protection alert if >5% of total requests hit fallback chain for >30m.
Response semantics: for admitted load-shed requests where we cannot return original semantics, return structured degrade with 'degrade_level' and correlation_id for client-side handling.
Rollout: feature-gated; start with internal tenants then 5 pilot customers before broad release.
risks: Incorrect cohort arithmetic could bias low-traffic tenants and accidentally expose more traffic than intended
Fallback to smaller models may change output quality leading to downstream product regressions; must connect to Redwood Optimize to run evaluation prompts pre-approval
Edge-case: dissolving back to 0% too quickly can cause flapping; hysteresis tuning required
Telemetry volume increase when instrumenting per-request fallback reasons may require retention/aggregation adjustments
implementation_plan: 1) Add trip detector library support in router service and runtime metrics exporter
2) Add cohort selection header and deterministic hashing for consistent routing
3) Implement fallback adapters in runtime with tenant checks against Tenant Catalog
4) Instrument telemetry and dashboards, add alerts and SLO protection metrics
5) Run staging chaos tests and internal canary for 24h
6) Pilot with two customers then gradual rollout with feature flag
tests: Unit tests for trip detector logic and hysteresis transitions
Integration tests simulating high p99 latency and error spikes to verify cohort progression
End-to-end staging test for multi-region failover where primary region is degraded and fallbacks obey data-residency rules
Chaos experiment: kill model-backend pods and observe safe dissolution and recovery behavior
rollout_plan: Internal exposure: enable for infra and internal tenants for 48 hours
Pilot: select 2 low-risk customers at 5% cohort for 72 hours
Expand: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over minimum 24h windows with SLO checks at each step
Rollback: immediate flag-off; automated alert if fallback invocations exceed 10% or SLO breach probability crosses 0.9
